source_caption:
M. Night Shyamalan specifically wanted Mel Gibson to star in Signs (2002) because he believed Gibson had the kind of presence that made audiences instantly trust him as someone who would do anything to protect his family. The role was a bit different from what Gibson usually played, since the character is quieter and more introspective than many of his earlier action roles. Gibson later said that once he started reading the script, he couldn’t put it down because the suspense pulled him in right from the beginning.

Another interesting choice was how the film was marketed. Shyamalan insisted that early posters avoid focusing too heavily on Gibson’s face, since he saw the film as an ensemble story rather than just a star vehicle. He also made sure the marketing didn’t lean on comparisons to The Sixth Sense, wanting audiences to see Signs as its own story rather than a repeat of his previous success.

Shyamalan has also mentioned that Signs was one of the easiest films he worked on in terms of writing and directing. The story came together quickly for him, and he felt confident about the tone and pacing from the very start, which helped shape the film’s steady tension and memorable suspense.

source_details.synopsis: Signs is a 2002 American science fiction horror thriller film written and directed by M. Night Shyamalan and produced by Shyamalan, Frank Marshall, Kathleen Kennedy and Sam Mercer. The film was produced by Touchstone Pictures, Blinding Edge Pictures and The Kennedy/Marshall Company. It was distributed by Buena Vista Pictures. Starring Mel Gibson and Joaquin Phoenix, the story focuses on a former Episcopal priest named Graham Hess who discovers a series of crop circles in his cornfield and that the phenomenon is a result of extraterrestrial life.
